en: The *Vasudhārā Dhāraṇī*:

Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Kauśāmbī, in the great and excellent forest known as Kaṇṭaka, together with a great community of monks consisting of about five hundred monks, and with a vast multitude of bodhisattva mahāsattvas who were endowed with all the qualities of the Buddha-dharma.
Now at that time, in the great city of Kauśāmbī, there lived a householder named Sucandra.
His senses were tranquil and his mind was serene; he had many sons and daughters, and was endowed with a large retinue of servants and attendants.
He was faithful, possessed of great faith, and having approached the Blessed One, he bowed at the Blessed One’s feet.
Having bowed his head to the Blessed One and circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times, he sat down to one side.
Seated there, the householder Sucandra addressed the Blessed One:
"I would ask the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, about a certain matter."
If the Blessed One would grant me the opportunity to answer the questions I have asked.
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the householder Sucandra: "Ask, householder, whatever you desire; I shall satisfy your mind according to what you ask.

When this had been said, the householder Sucandra spoke thus to the Blessed One: "How, Blessed One, does a son of good family or a daughter of good family, having become poor, become no longer poor, or having become ill..."
And having become so, one becomes free from disease.
Then the Blessed One, although already knowing, said this to the householder Sucandra: "Householder, why do you ask a question concerning the absence of poverty?"

When this had been said, the householder Sucandra addressed the Blessed One as follows: "I am poor, Blessed One; I have many dependents, many sons, and many daughters. Therefore, may the Blessed One teach that Dharma-discourse by which poor beings might become no longer poor, becoming endowed with abundant wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses, and being beloved and pleasing."

May they be pleasing to behold; may they be lords of generosity, great lords of generosity; may they possess inexhaustible gold, bullion, wealth, grain, jewels, treasuries, and granaries, and be enriched with gems, pearls, diamonds, conch shells, crystals, coral, gold, and silver;
and may they have well-established houses, sons, wives, and households.
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the householder Sucandra: "In the past, householder, long ago..."
At that time, there was a Blessed One, a Tathāgata, Arhat, and perfectly enlightened Buddha named Vajradharasāgaranirghoṣa.
...the charioteer of men, the teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One; from the presence of that Tathāgata ...
... those [teachings] were upheld, recited, mastered, rejoiced in, and extensively proclaimed to others.
4 /// ... neither humans cause them harm, nor non-humans cause them harm, nor yakṣas cause them harm...
...they cause them to be established. In this way, the *kuṃbhāṇḍas*, *austārakas*, *pūtanās*, *kaṭapūtanās*, and *yātudhānas* [do not ...]
They do not cause harm— whether by taking away [possessions], by taking away flavors, by taking away what has been born, or by taking away flowing water—
for one whose house [is protected by this].
... [this] has come to the hearing, been mastered, recited, retained, rejoiced in, and extensively proclaimed to others.
...it will lead to happiness, security, abundance, and well-being for her; and whoever [protects] this earth...
At midnight, three times or four times, the deities, being delighted, will come in person and let fall a rain of grain.
They are pleased by the designation of the Saṅgha and pleased by the intention of the Dharma-preacher.
Homage to Vajradharasāgaranirghoṣa!
... for me, acaphame, acapame;
the uprooter, the opener.
Ucchedani; Sasyavati; Dhānyā;
Surūpā; Amalā; Ananastā; Vinanastā; Viśvakeśī.
Paṃkure saṃkure / khakhare khakhame / dhudhume /
tara tara tara / vajra vajra vajropame kaṭe kaṭe / ukke nukke varṣaṇī niṣpādani /
Recall the Tathāgata Vajradharasāgaranirghoṣa! Remember, remember!
Recall the truth of all the Tathāgatas!
Recall the truth of the Saṅgha!
Taṭa taṭa! Pūra pūra!
Fulfill, fulfill!
Grant all the hopes of me, Dāmasiṃha; O nourisher, O auspicious one, O you of peaceful mind!
O Mahāmati, Maṅgalamati, Subhadramati, come! Remember the pledge! Svāhā!
Recall the conduct; svāhā!
Recall the foundation, svāhā!
Recall the majestic power, svāhā!
Recall steadfastness, svāhā!
Recall victory, svāhā!
Recall the victory over all sentient beings; svāhā!
Householder, this is that dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā. By the power of this dhāraṇī, diseases, famine, pestilence, wildernesses, and the like do not prevail.

Householder, whoever, having performed worship to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones, should recite these mantra-words of the Vasudhārā-dhāraṇī for a single night, for them there shall be a stream [of wealth] as large as a great man.

It completely fills the house with all kinds of grain, all utensils, and it destroys all calamities; therefore, householder, you should take up this Vasudhārā Dhāraṇī, preserve it, recite it, and teach it.
"And reveal it in detail to others;
that will be for your long-term welfare, benefit, and happiness. "Excellent, Blessed One!
Having heard this Vasudhārā Dhāraṇī from the presence of the Blessed One, the householder Sucandra was thrilled, satisfied, and elated.

With a joyful heart, delighted and filled with gladness and happiness, he prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One and said this to him: "I have grasped the Vasudhārā Dhāraṇī; it has been humbled, retained, recited, and mastered. Now I shall proclaim it in detail to others."

Then the householder Sucandra circumambulated the Blessed One many hundreds of thousands of times, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, and, without looking back at the Blessed One again, departed from the Blessed One's presence. Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda.

"Go, Ānanda, and having gone to the residence of the householder Sucandra, observe its appearance: whether it is complete, abundant in wealth and grain, and rich in jewels; and whether the great treasuries and storehouses are filled with all necessary utensils.
Then the Venerable Ānanda, having seen the residence of the householder Sucandra, was struck with wonder and filled with joy and gladness.

He said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, by which the householder Sucandra has become so immensely wealthy, possessed of great enjoyments, and enriched with vast treasuries and granaries?
The Blessed One replied:

Ānanda, the householder Sucandra was faithful, supremely devout, and possessed of a virtuous intention; he upheld, maintained, recited, mastered, and extensively proclaimed to others this Vasudhārā Dhāraṇī.
Therefore, Ānanda, you too should take up this Vasudhārā Dhāraṇī, uphold it, and cause others to grasp it.
Recite it,
master it,
and reveal it in detail to others.

That will be for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, and for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of a great multitude of beings, including gods and humans. Ānanda, I do not perceive anyone in this world— with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins,
gods, humans, and asuras— who could make this dhāraṇī otherwise.
Or that it will pass [them] by—this is impossible.

Why is that? Because, Ānanda, these dhāraṇī mantra-words are indeed indestructible; they will not even come to the range of hearing for those beings whose roots of merit are exhausted, let alone being committed to a book, or held in the heart, or maintained [in memory].

For what reason? This speech belongs to all the Tathāgatas; this dhāraṇī has been spoken by all the Tathāgatas, empowered, sealed with the seal of Dharma, rejoiced in, revealed, manifested, praised, extolled, proclaimed, disclosed, made clear, and declared for the benefit of all sentient beings who are poor, afflicted by disease, and oppressed by all fears and calamities.
He said, "Blessed One, I have grasped this Vasudhārā Dhāraṇī; it has been retained, recited, mastered, and well-internalized by my mind."
Then, at that time, the venerable Ānanda rose from his seat and, with palms joined in reverence, uttered this inspired utterance:
O Blessed One, the Buddhas are inconceivable, and the Buddha-qualities are also inconceivable.
For those who have deep faith in what is inconceivable, the maturation is said to be inconceivable.
